radiology_notes.text:
INDICATION:  ___ man with dyspnea.

Comparison is made to the prior study of ___.

UPRIGHT RADIOGRAPH OF THE CHEST:  The heart size is mildly enlarged.  Mild
hilar contour prominence is noted.  There is increased prominence of
interstitial marking of the lungs suggesting the presence of superimposed
pulmonary edema on underlying emphysema.  The pacemaker lead is unchanged with
tip terminating within the right ventricle.

INDICATION:  ___ man with shortness of breath and abdominal pain.

Comparison is made to the prior CT of the abdomen ___ and CTA of
the chest of ___.

TECHNIQUE:  Axial MDCT images of the torso were obtained after administration
of 100 cc of Optiray intravenously.  Multiplanar reformatted images were
obtained.

CT OF THE CHEST:  No filling defect is noted within the main pulmonary artery
and branches to suggest pulmonary embolism.  The aorta does not demonstrate
any acute pathology.  No pleural or pericardial effusion is noted.  The
pacemaker leads are in place.  The lungs demonstrate centrilobular and
paraseptal emphysematous changes with superimposed foci of ground-glass
density, most prominent at the lung apices.  There is also septal thickening
at the lung bases.  The findings are compatible with superimposed pulmonary
edema and the underlying emphysema.  Note is made of multiple pathologically
enlarged mediastinal nodes since prior study.  The nodes are located within
the right paratracheal space, anterior precarinal space, subcarinal location
and prevascular space.  The largest node in the subcarinal location measures
24 mm in short axis.  The node in the anterior precarinal space measures 22
mm.  There is diffuse thickening along the right mainstem bronchus extending
into the bronchus intermedius.

CT OF THE ABDOMEN:  The liver, spleen, and adrenal glands have normal
appearance.  The gallbladder contains stone with no signs of cholecystitis.
The pancreas and the stomach, duodenum, loops of small bowel and large bowel
have normal appearance.  Both kidneys contain multiple small hypodense areas
which are too small to characterize.  There is mild ectasia and tortuosity of
the aorta but no definite aneurysm is noted.  The patient is status post
repair of infrarenal abdominal aortic aneurysm.  The aorta is unchanged in
appearance with no evidence of intramural hematoma or other acute pathology.
There are two right renal arteries.  No free air or fluid is noted within the
abdomen.  No pathologically enlarged nodes are noted.

CT OF THE PELVIS:  The urinary bladder, distal ureters, rectum and sigmoid
colon have normal appearance.

BONE WINDOWS:  No concerning lytic or sclerotic lesions are identified.

IMPRESSION:

1.  No evidence of acute aortic pathology.  No pulmonary embolism.

2.  Cholelithiasis.

3.  Pulmonary edema superimposed on emphysema.

4.  Multiple pathologically enlarged mediastinal nodes and questionable
thickening of the right bronchus intermedius. If further evaluation is
required, dedicated chest CT is recommended.

COMPARISON:  ___.

FINDINGS:  As compared to the previous radiograph, there is no relevant
change.  The pre-existing right basal opacities are minimally improved. 
Otherwise, constant appearance of lungs and heart.
